question:
A confined run terminates normally and reports convergence. Which interpretations of its head
profile and water budget are appropriate? (Select ALL correct answers.)
success:
Correct. CHD maintains head through calculated exchange flows. The steady-state inflows and outflows
should balance within numerical closure. The confined profile is potentiometric. Agreement with an
applicable analytical solution supports numerical verification; it does not validate the conceptual
model or parameters against a real aquifer.
error:
Not quite. Check the prescribed boundary heads, the meaning of the confined profile, and the water
balance separately. An analytical reference can test the numerical solution only when its
assumptions apply. Neither numerical convergence nor analytical agreement establishes that the model
represents a real aquifer correctly.

question:
Suppose you tighten PCG HCLOSE from 10⁻⁴ m to 10⁻⁵ m, keep RCLOSE and all other settings unchanged,
and obtain the same iteration count. Which explanations or conclusions are valid? (Select ALL
correct answers.)
success:
Correct. An iteration can reduce the head change below both thresholds, or the residual criterion
can govern when PCG stops. Therefore, a tighter HCLOSE does not have to increase the iteration
count. HCLOSE concerns iterative head changes, not error relative to an exact continuous solution or
to the real aquifer.
error:
Not quite. Consider which stopping condition actually limits convergence. The original run may
already satisfy the tighter head criterion by the time the residual criterion is met. Also
distinguish a head-change threshold from a bound on solution error.

question:
You refine the grid from 51 to 501 cells while keeping the CHD-centre distance at 5,000 m, the width
unchanged, and the recharge rate at 150 mm/year. In this app, recharge is excluded from both CHD
cells. Which statements are correct? (Select ALL correct answers.)
success:
Correct. Cell-centre spacing is L/(N−1). Because the two CHD cells receive no recharge, the total
recharged length is (N−2)Δx = L−Δx: 4,900 m for 51 cells and 4,990 m for 501 cells. A fixed recharge
rate therefore does not imply identical integrated recharge. Compare heads at the same physical
coordinates.
error:
Not quite. Distinguish the recharge rate per unit area from the total recharge flow. Check which
cell areas actually receive recharge. Also use physical coordinates when comparing grids; a cell
index has a different spatial meaning after refinement.

question:
In this lab, the confined case uses top 0 m and bottom −20 m. Switching to the convertible case with
top 30 m changes the bottom to 0 m. With K unchanged, which conclusions are correct? (Select ALL
correct answers.)
success:
Correct. In the confined case, transmissivity is based on a fixed thickness of 20 m. In the
convertible case, wet cells below the top have a head-dependent saturated thickness; cells at or
above the top are fully saturated. The app also changes the layer bottom, so differences between the
two head profiles cannot be attributed solely to the numerical solver.
error:
Not quite. Transmissivity depends on saturated thickness as well as K. Compare the aquifer geometry
in the two setups and locate the calculated head relative to the top and bottom. The aquifer top is
a geometric input, not a prescribed interior head.

question:
Suppose repeated runs display small differences in elapsed time even when their input settings are
unchanged. Which procedures support a defensible comparison of the experiment's numerical
performance? (Select ALL correct answers.)
success:
Correct. Controlled settings and repeated timings support a fair comparison. Distinguish inner
linear iterations from outer updates, and compare the same reported quantities. This app's elapsed
time includes native program startup, solution, and output, so very small timing differences need
not reflect differences in solver arithmetic.
error:
Not quite. Separate a repeatable performance difference from ordinary timing variability, and verify
that the compared runs use comparable numerical settings. Counts with different meanings, such as
inner and outer iterations, cannot be substituted for one another.

question:
After inspecting the solver choices in this Solver Lab, which statements correctly describe the
implemented combinations? (Select ALL correct answers.)
success:
Correct. The outer treatment of nonlinear equations and the inner linear-solution method are
different choices. MODFLOW-NWT retains its Newton formulation when its linear method changes.
Although MODFLOW 6 can support other formulations, this lab's current setup uses Picard with IMS.
MODFLOW-2005 offers PCG and SIP in the lab.
error:
Not quite. Do not infer the nonlinear formulation from the engine's age or from the name of its
inner linear solver. Identify the method implemented by this app: Newton in MODFLOW-NWT and Picard
in its current MODFLOW 6 configuration.
